# Assignment

### 1. Choice Operators (10 pts)

```{r}
w <- 10.2
x <- 1.3
y <- 2.8
z <- 17.5
colors <- c("red", "blue", "green")
masses <- c(45.2, 36.1, 27.8, 81.6, 42.4)
```

1a
```{r}
# a. "green" is in `colors`
"green" %in% colors
```

1b
```{r}
# b. "purple" is not in `colors`
!("purple" %in% colors)
```

1c
```{r}
# c. Each value in `masses` is greater than 40.
masses > 40
```

1d
```{r}
# d. `w` is greater than `x`, or `y` is greater than `z`
w > x | y > z
```

1e
```{r}
# e.  `x` times `w` is between 13.2 and 13.5
13.2 < x * w & x * w < 13.5
```

### 2. Using `dplyr` Choice Functions (20 points)

```{r}
#| message: false
library(dplyr)
library(lterdatasampler)
```

2a
```{r}
crab_size <- 17

if_else(crab_size >= 20, "large", "small")
```

2b
```{r}
case_when(crab_size >= 20 ~ "large",
          crab_size >= 10 ~ "medium",
          .default = "small")
```

2c
```{r}
pie_crab %>%
  mutate(size_category = if_else(size >= 20, "large", "small"), .after = size)
```

2d
```{r}
pie_crab %>%
  mutate(size_category3 = case_when(size >= 20 ~ "large",
                                    size >= 10 ~ "medium",
                                    .default = "small"), .after = size)
```

### 3. If/Else Statements (20 points)

3a
```{r}
age_class <- "adult"
if (age_class == "sapling"){
  y <- 10
} else if (age_class == "seedling") {
  y <- 5
} else {
  y <- 0
}
y
```

3b
```{r}
get_y_from_age_class <- function(age_class){
  if (age_class == "sapling"){
    y <- 10
  } else if (age_class == "seedling") {
    y <- 5
  } else {
    y <- 0
  }
  return(y)
}

get_y_from_age_class("sapling")
get_y_from_age_class("seedling")
get_y_from_age_class("adult")
get_y_from_age_class("mature")
get_y_from_age_class("established")
```

3c
```{r}
prediction <- function(x){
  if (x > 0 & x < 15){
    y <- 6 + 0.8 * x
  } else if (x >= 15 & x < 30) {
    y <- 5 + 0.75 * x
  } else {
    y <- NA
  }
  return(y)
}

prediction(5)
prediction(26)
prediction(-2)
```

### 4. Size Estimates by Name (20 points)

```{r}
get_mass_from_length <- function(a, b, length){
  mass <- a * length ^ b
  return(mass)
}

get_mass_from_length_by_name <- function(length, name){
  if (name == "Stegosauria"){
    a <- 10.95
    b <- 2.64
  } else if (name == "Theropoda"){
    a <- 0.73
    b <- 3.63
  } else if (name == "Sauropoda"){
    a <- 214.44
    b <- 1.46
  } else {
    return(NA)
  }
  get_mass_from_length(a, b, length)
}
```

4a
```{r}
get_mass_from_length_by_name(10, "Stegosauria")
```

4b
```{r}
get_mass_from_length_by_name(8, "Theropoda")
```

4c
```{r}
get_mass_from_length_by_name(12, "Sauropoda")
```

4d
```{r}
get_mass_from_length_by_name(13, "Ankylosauria")
```

Challenge 1 (optional)
```{r}
get_mass_from_length_by_name <- function(length, name){
  if (name == "Stegosauria"){
    a <- 10.95
    b <- 2.64
  } else if (name == "Theropoda"){
    a <- 0.73
    b <- 3.63
  } else if (name == "Sauropoda"){
    a <- 214.44
    b <- 1.46
  } else {

}

get_mass_from_length_by_name(13, "Ankylosauria")
```

Challenge 2 (optional)

```{r}
get_mass_from_length_by_name <- function(length, name){
  if (name == "Stegosauria"){
    # nested if-else: equation depends on length
    if (length > 8){
      a <- 10.95
      b <- 2.64
    } else {
      a <- 8.5
      b <- 2.8
    }
  } else if (name == "Theropoda"){
    a <- 0.73
    b <- 3.63
  } else if (name == "Sauropoda"){
    a <- 214.44
    b <- 1.46
  } else {
    warning(paste("No known estimation for", name))
    return(NA)
  }
  get_mass_from_length(a, b, length)
}

get_mass_from_length_by_name(6, "Stegosauria")
```

### 5. Putting It All Together: Portal Rodents (30 points)

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)

surveys <- read_csv("data/surveys.csv")
species <- read_csv("data/species.csv")
```

5a
```{r}
rodents <- surveys %>%
  left_join(species, by = "species_id") %>%
  filter(taxa == "Rodent") %>%
  mutate(scientific_name = str_c(genus, species, sep = " "))

head(rodents)
```

5b
```{r}
# the . needs to be escaped (or use fixed("sp.")); otherwise "sp." matches
# any "sp" followed by any character, such as "spectabilis" or "spilosoma"
rodents <- rodents %>%
  mutate(id_level = if_else(str_detect(scientific_name, "sp\\."),
                            "genus only", "species"))

rodents %>%
  count(id_level)
```

5c
```{r}
rodents <- rodents %>%
  mutate(season = if_else(month %in% 4:9, "warm", "cool"))
```

5d
```{r}
rodents <- rodents %>%
  mutate(weight_class = case_when(is.na(weight) ~ "unknown",
                                  weight < 20 ~ "small",
                                  weight < 50 ~ "medium",
                                  .default = "large"))

rodents %>%
  count(weight_class)
```

Without the "unknown" line, individuals with missing weights would be classified as "large." `weight < 20` and `weight < 50` both return `NA` when `weight` is `NA`, and `case_when` treats `NA` like `FALSE`, so those rows fall all the way through to the `.default` value.

5e
```{r}
rodents %>%
  filter(weight_class != "unknown") %>%
  count(year, season, weight_class) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = n, color = weight_class)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ season) +
  labs(x = "Year",
       y = "Number of Individuals",
       color = "Weight Class") +
  theme_classic()
```

Answers will vary. Any accurate description of a pattern in the plot (e.g., which weight class is most common, how counts change over time, or differences between seasons) is acceptable.

### 6. Challenge: A "Safe" Tidyverse Function (OPTIONAL)

```{r}
categorize_by_threshold <- function(df, col, threshold){
  values <- pull(df, {{ col }})

  if (!is.numeric(values)) {
    stop("Column must be numeric.")
  } else if (threshold < min(values, na.rm = TRUE) |
             threshold > max(values, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    stop(paste("Threshold must be between",
               min(values, na.rm = TRUE), "and", max(values, na.rm = TRUE)))
  } else {
    df %>%
      mutate(category = if_else({{ col }} >= threshold, "above", "below"))
  }
}
```

6a
```{r}
categorize_by_threshold(rodents, weight, 50) %>%
  select(species_id, weight, category)
```

6b
```{r}
categorize_by_threshold(rodents, hindfoot_length, 30) %>%
  select(species_id, hindfoot_length, category)
```

6c
```{r}
#| error: true
categorize_by_threshold(rodents, genus, 50)
```

6d
```{r}
#| error: true
categorize_by_threshold(rodents, weight, 500)
```
